evidence: no deterministic engine for strategy_id 'trend_pullback_call_v1' (engine-registered: current_control_v1, directional_spread_v1, range_hv_iron_condor_v1)
expected_failure_modes: Regime flip immediately after entry: TREND_HV can decay into RANGE_HV or RANGE_LV within days, turning a momentum continuation into a theta bleed or a repeated-stop chop.
The pullback is actually the start of a reversal; repeated 1% structure-based stop-outs accumulate faster than the occasional winner, producing negative expectancy.
The VIX premium cap excludes too many valid trending setups, collapsing the trade count below the 20-trade minimum and forcing a NOT_RELIABLE classification.
ADX in high-volatility regimes is lagging and noisy, admitting entries that look like strong trends but immediately mean-revert.
hypothesis: In TREND_HV regimes, high-volatility trending markets show momentum persistence; continuation moves after a controlled pullback are more reliable than breakout entries, which suffer from false breakouts and poor fills. Buying an ATM call on a pullback to the 20-EMA while the uptrend structure stays intact (spot above EMA50, EMA20 above EMA50, ADX confirming trend strength, RSI cooled into a neutral band) prices the entry closer to support, reducing the distance to the structure- based stop. Capping the VIX premium zone below RICH/HIGH/PANIC keeps long-premium theta bleed manageable, since expensive implied vol typically reverts and damages long premium even if spot moves in the direction of the trade.
research_question: Over the frozen window (2025-08-13..2026-08-13), does a TREND_HV-only pullback long call on NIFTY - defined as spot above EMA50, EMA20 above EMA50, ADX > 25, RSI in 45..55, VIX_ZONE not RICH/HIGH/PANIC and PCR <= 1.1 - produce a positive net expectancy with at least 20 trades on the out-of-sample slice (exits on/after 2026-03-01), and does it differ materially from the current_control_v1 baseline?
title: Trend-persistence pullback long call (TREND_HV, VIX-capped)
